clue.text: Intuitive type, yet needing time with textbook

parts.note: yet in the sense 'nevertheless' is a synonym of though
a reader is a school textbook of passages for reading practice

explanation.surface: Someone who works by instinct still has to spend hours with a textbook.
explanation.definitionFit: A mind-reader seems to know others' thoughts by intuition, so is an intuitive type.

clue.text: Steal, packing to leave hotel? Give oneself up

definitions.meaning: a guest packing to check out might slip the hotel's bath linen into the case, a cheeky theft
to concede defeat, as a boxer's corner signals surrender

explanation.surface: A guest pockets things while packing to check out, then surrenders.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom, from boxing, means to admit defeat and give up the fight; read literally it is tossing a towel into a suitcase.

clue.text: The first to offer a tremendous example — self-sacrifice

definitions.text: The first to offer a tremendous example — self-sacrifice

indicators.note: the opening letter of each word that follows is to be taken in turn

explanation.surface: Someone was the first to set a tremendous example of giving up their own life for others.
explanation.walkthrough: Captain Lawrence Oates, on Scott's 1912 Antarctic expedition, walked out into a blizzard so as not to slow his companions: a famous act of self-sacrifice, which the whole clue describes.
explanation.definitionFit: Captain Oates is the classic British example of self-sacrifice, having walked to his death to help his comrades.

clue.text: Respectful behaviour from queues in part of theatre

indicators.note: the queues are placed inside the theatre part

parts.note: the gods are the highest gallery seats in a theatre
lines are queues of people waiting

explanation.surface: Polite conduct shown by people queuing in a section of the theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: Godliness is piety, devout and reverent behaviour towards God.

clue.text: One's so happy to shoot off for no reason

definitions.text: One's so happy to shoot off for no reason

parts.words: One's so happy to shoot off for no reason
parts.note: someone 'happy' with this firearm part is reckless, firing without cause; the clue describes the thing that is linked to that phrase

explanation.surface: Someone is so cheerful they rush off without any reason.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom trigger-happy describes someone who shoots too readily, so this gun part is what such a person is happy with.

clue.text: Universal approval as European left in boat

indicators.note: the left letter goes inside the boat

parts.note: a cat is a catamaran or a type of sailing boat

explanation.surface: A European sailor left in a boat wins everyone's applause.
explanation.definitionFit: Eclat is brilliant success or acclaim, the applause of all.

clue.text: From Hades, demon attacking tragic heroine

indicators.note: the answer is taken from within the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A devil out of the underworld assails a heroine of tragedy.
explanation.definitionFit: Desdemona is Othello's wife in Shakespeare's tragedy, murdered by him.

clue.text: Carroll achieved curious version of poet

indicators.note: a curious version is an odd rearrangement of the clue words

explanation.surface: Lewis Carroll produced a strange version of some poet's work.
explanation.definitionFit: Richard Lovelace was a 17th-century Cavalier poet, author of To Althea, from Prison.

clue.text: Not at all sweet, in black depression

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
a rut is a groove or hollow in the ground

explanation.surface: Someone sour and down in a black mood.
explanation.definitionFit: Brut describes the driest champagne, with almost no sweetness.

clue.text: Physician not doing well in practice

parts.note: DR is the abbreviation for doctor
ill means unwell, not doing well

explanation.surface: A sick doctor in a medical practice.
explanation.definitionFit: Drill is repetitive practice or training exercise.

clue.text: It's something to don, about to get into Oxford

definitions.text: It's something to don, about to get into Oxford

parts.words: It's something to don, about to get into Oxford
parts.note: Oxford here is a laced shoe, not the university; the garment is put on just before the foot goes into the shoe

explanation.surface: Something for an academic to wear, a candidate about to be admitted to Oxford.
explanation.walkthrough: 'don' and 'Oxford' suggest the university and its tutors; in fact 'don' means put on and an Oxford is a style of shoe.
explanation.definitionFit: A sock is worn on the foot and goes on before a shoe such as an Oxford.

clue.text: I keep quiet during jazz music cutting through the air

indicators.note: the letters for 'I keep quiet' come in the middle of the jazz

parts.note: swing is a style of big-band jazz
SH is the call to be quiet

explanation.surface: Someone stays silent while the jazz plays and something slices the air.
explanation.definitionFit: Swishing describes a whooshing movement through the air, like a cane or tail.

clue.text: Next, providing opening for scholar in Greek

indicators.note: the first word opens up to make room for the scholar

parts.note: then means next, after that
BA, Bachelor of Arts, is a graduate scholar

explanation.surface: Next, an opening is offered to a scholar of Greek.
explanation.definitionFit: A Theban is a native of Thebes, a city of ancient Greece, hence a Greek.

clue.text: Stick aristocrat's taken to cattle, we hear

indicators.note: the result is what we hear spoken, not how it is written

parts.note: a nob is a toff or aristocrat; Kerry is an Irish breed of cattle; together they say NOBKERRY

explanation.surface: An aristocrat has taken a stick to his cattle, so we are told.
explanation.definitionFit: A knobkerrie is a short wooden club with a knobbed head, used in southern Africa.

clue.text: Pop group to keep waving in fashionable cause

parts.note: a band is a pop group
to wag on is to keep on wagging, waving to and fro

explanation.surface: A pop group tries to stay waving the flag for a trendy cause.
explanation.definitionFit: A bandwagon is a popular movement or cause that people join because it is fashionable.

clue.text: One may demand extra time to find weapon, perhaps

definitions.meaning: a late goal levelling the score in a cup match can force the game into extra time
in slang, a gun or other weapon that evens up the odds

explanation.surface: A player may need extra time to find a weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: An equaliser is a levelling goal in football and also slang for a gun.

clue.text: Likelihood of sailor having to keep two daughters?

indicators.note: the sailor holds the daughters inside

parts.note: OS, ordinary seaman, is a sailor
D is the abbreviation for daughter, so two give DD

explanation.surface: How likely is it that a sailor will have to support two daughters?
explanation.definitionFit: Odds express the likelihood or probability of something happening.

clue.text: Have success restraining horse in some furze

indicators.note: the success word holds the horse letter in

parts.note: to win is to have success
H stands for heroin, slang name horse

explanation.surface: Someone manages to hold back a horse in some gorse bushes.
explanation.definitionFit: Whin is another name for gorse, the spiny shrub also called furze.

clue.text: In close-up, art turned out better

indicators.note: the letters of the words are turned out into a new order

explanation.surface: Seen in close-up, a piece of art turned out to be superior.
explanation.walkthrough: 'better' looks like the comparative of good; it is one who bets.
explanation.definitionFit: A speculator gambles on markets, so is one who bets: a better.

clue.text: One found in volcanic crater may be inconsistent

indicators.note: the one is placed within the rearranged letters
volcanic suggests an eruption, a violent rearrangement of the word

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Something discovered inside a volcano's crater may behave irregularly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'volcanic' turns CRATER into ERRATC; 'found in' puts I inside that to give ERRATIC. An erratic is also a boulder carried by ice, which suits the volcanic scene.
explanation.definitionFit: Erratic means irregular and unpredictable, so inconsistent.

clue.text: Was long embarrassed, being drunk

definitions.meaning: to stew is to fret or suffer discomfort for a long time, as in stew in one's own juice

explanation.surface: Someone stayed mortified for ages because they were drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: Stewed is past tense of stew, to suffer long anxiety, and also slang for drunk.

clue.text: In tubing, find a piece of gold

indicators.note: the A goes inside the tubing

parts.note: a duct is a tube or pipe

explanation.surface: Someone finds a gold nugget inside some piping.
explanation.definitionFit: A ducat was a gold coin once used across Europe, so a piece of gold.

clue.text: Set free from financial commitment, when overdrawn

definitions.meaning: a lease is a financial commitment; drawn up over again, it is let once more

explanation.surface: Someone is freed from debts when their account is overdrawn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overdrawn' suggests a bank account in the red; here it means drawn up again, so the property is leased a second time.
explanation.definitionFit: Released means freed, and read as re-leased it means let again under a new lease.

clue.text: A month working conveyor belt

parts.note: APR is the abbreviation for April
on means working, operating

explanation.surface: A conveyor belt has been running for a month.
explanation.definitionFit: An apron is a type of conveyor made of overlapping plates, used to carry material.

clue.text: Gulp as 11 has bone knocked out

indicators.note: the bone is removed from the word

parts.note: the answer to clue 11 across
the shin is the shinbone, the tibia

explanation.surface: A drinker's gulp as someone has a bone knocked out.
explanation.definitionFit: A swig is a large swallow or gulp of drink.

clue.text: English tucked into marmalades — they were delicious

indicators.note: the English letter goes inside the cats

parts.note: marmalade cats are ginger-striped cats

explanation.surface: An English person eats marmalades and finds them delicious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'marmalades' seem to be preserves; they are ginger cats.
explanation.definitionFit: Cates is an archaic word for delicacies or dainty foods, things that were delicious.

clue.text: Path taken through the water in sound

indicators.note: the spoken form is meant; a sound is also a strait of water, adding to the surface

parts.note: rowed means propelled through water by oars

explanation.surface: A route taken by rowing boat across a sound.
explanation.definitionFit: A road is a route or way, so a path.

clue.text: For example, extreme right fingernail cut badly

indicators.note: something done badly is mangled, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A fingernail clipped badly on the far right side.
explanation.definitionFit: The extreme right is an example of a political lunatic fringe, the fanatical edge of a movement.
